text:
incident-bot: P0 — Multiple customer-facing errors observed in eu-west-1. Routing spillover triggered fallback; elevated 502s and token latency > 2s for several routes. Pager to @Ryan. Please acknowledge and start triage.

Ryan: Ack. I’m on-call and looking at the console now. Any immediate mitigation suggested?

Jamie: Noted — seeing a spike in routing queue depth and a bunch of requests targeting fallback-model-v1-quant. Looks like autoscaler bumped down some dedicated pools and routing spilled to fallback tiers.

Sanjay: grabbing logs from the routing-router instances. Prelim grep shows misroute decisions around 2024-11-10T14:23Z. Query: were we doing any canary rollouts in EU at that time?

Olivia: No active canaries in eu-west-1. There was an automated capacity reclamation window at 14:20Z (reserved capacity reclaim job). Could be related.

Ryan: Impact scope — which customers/routes? Any billing/paid-customer outages?

Jamie: Affected routes: /v1/generate (tier: gold & silver) in eu-west-1. Some requests fell back to fallback-model-v1-quant which is not compatible with the higher-tier prompt transformers — produced format errors and 502s.

Sanjay: Pasting key routing decisions from routing-proxy log (redacted ids):
```
2024-11-10T14:22:41Z routeId=svc-124 decision=spillover -> tier=fallback-model-v1-quant reason=capacity_shortfall
2024-11-10T14:22:42Z routeId=svc-125 decision=spillover -> tier=fallback-model-v1-quant reason=capacity_shortfall
2024-11-10T14:22:43Z routeId=svc-126 decision=route-mismatch -> tier=fallback-model-v1-quant reason=model_incompatible
```

Olivia: The weird bit is the model_compatibility check — fallback-model-v1-quant should be flagged as incompatible for gold prompts. Looks like our model-compat rules were not applied after the spillover policy executed.

Jamie: Hypothesis 1: reclaim job reduced dedicated capacity under threshold, spillover policy opted for quick-compat fallback but policy evaluation lost model_compat constraints due to a cache TTL bug.

Sanjay: Hypothesis 2: routing policy version mismatch between control-plane and regional proxies — control plane had latest policy (with strict compatibility), proxies still had v2 that allowed fallback selection without compatibility check.

Ryan: Mitigation suggestion — temporarily freeze spillover and pin routes to dedicated pools where available, and scale up a small burst pool to buy time. Can someone run command to mute spillover in eu-west-1?

Alex: I can patch routing-policy at control plane to disable spillover for eu-west-1 for 10m. Command I’ll run: `redwoodctl routes update --region eu-west-1 --spillover false --reason "incident: freeze spillover"`

Jamie: Also manually pin the gold routes to their dedicated pool: `redwoodctl routes pin --route /v1/generate --pool dedicated-eu-gold`

Sanjay: Executed pin for 3/4 affected services. Scaling a small burst pool now: `infractl pool create --region eu-west-1 --type burst --gpus 2 --ttl 30m`.

Olivia: After the freeze and pins, metrics show error rate falling — 502s down from 8% to 0.7% in 3m. Latency back to baseline ~120ms for pinned routes.

Ryan: Great. Can we capture timeline and artifacts for RCA? We need exact policy versions, agent logs, and the reclaim job schedule.

Jamie: Attaching artifacts (links):
- routing-proxy logs: https://s3.redwood/internal/logs/2349999999-routing-proxy.log
- control-plane policy history: https://console.redwood/policies/history?region=eu-west-1&since=2024-11-10T14:00Z
- reclaim job runbook: https://confluence.redwood/display/infra/capacity-reclaim

Sanjay: I’ve uploaded a filtered log bundle to the incident folder: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2349999999/bundle.tar.gz (includes proxy logs, model registry events, and autoscaler traces)

Olivia: Quick check of model-registry events shows fallback-model-v1-quant was recently promoted to a "fast-fallback" tag in the registry two days ago — that could explain why it was considered a candidate in the fallback set despite incompatibility.

Jamie: So combined hypothesis: (A) capacity reclaim reduced dedicated capacity, (B) spillover policy triggered and consulted fallback set that included fast-fallback models, (C) a policy propagation/cache bug or version skew allowed fallback selection without re-checking model_compat, resulting in misroute to quantized model, causing format/502 errors.

Sanjay: To test propagation skew hypothesis — checking control-plane -> proxy push logs: found push failure at 14:21:58Z with transient 504; retries happened, but proxies accepted an older cached policy until 14:23:05Z.

Ryan: That aligns with the timing of errors. Next steps for in-incident RCA: collect patch window, exact policy commit hashes, proxy versions, and any TTLs for policy caches. Also produce a definitive customer impact list and estimated affected requests.

Jamie: Action items being tracked: 
1) Jamie — assemble timeline (complete) and collect policy commit IDs.
2) Sanjay — extract exact request IDs and export sample error payloads (in progress).
3) Olivia — check model-registry tag history and revert fast-fallback tagging if needed (done).
4) Alex — follow up to roll back spillover freeze after safe autoscale (monitoring).

Alex: I’ll keep the freeze for 15m and then coordinate a controlled re-enable with canary flags.

Ryan: Communication — notify affected customers with short blurb: we experienced short routing spillover that caused degraded responses in EU, mitigated within ~10m, root cause under investigation. Please draft a customer notify.

Jamie: Draft ready — short message + personal contacts for enterprise customers. Posting to #customer-notify after sign-off.

Sanjay: For the formal RCA, we'll include: sequence timeline, logs (proxy/controlplane/autoscaler), root cause hypotheses, and mitigation plan: 
- Fix: enforce model_compat check in proxy evaluation code path (hotfix).
- Fix: improve policy push reliability and add stronger backfill/validation on proxies.
- Fix: add guardrail to prevent fast-fallback tags being applied to incompatible models.

Olivia: I’ll open PR for the hotfix to short-circuit fallback selection if compatibility check absent. Linking PR: https://git.redwood/p/infra/routing/+/5678

Ryan: OK team — once we have artifacts and PRs linked, we’ll convert this thread into the postmortem and schedule a follow-up 1:1 with product to assess SLA/customer credits. Thanks for fast ops.

incident-bot: Incident resolved — mitigation verified at 2024-11-10T14:35Z. Postmortem required. Incident severity: P0 -> upgraded to RCA required.

Jamie: Closing handoff to postmortem owners: Jamie (lead), Sanjay (logs), Olivia (fixes), Alex (deployment/ops). Please add any missing items in the postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood/display/pm/eu-spillover-fallback-2024-11-10

Ryan: Thanks all. Good triage and safe mitigation.
